вижду: видѣти — I see (1st sg. pres.); with не, 'I no longer see'
власти: власть — might, power(s) (gen. sg. in unit 1, object of negated вижду; acc. pl. in unit 28, 'seize power(s) for yourselves')
сильнаго: сильный — strong, mighty (gen. sg., agreeing with брата)
богатаго: богатый — rich (gen. sg., agreeing with брата)
многовои: многовои — many-warriored, thronged with warriors (gen. sg., agreeing with брата); a compound adjective (много 'many' + вои 'warriors')
моего: мой — my (gen. sg., agreeing with брата)
ярослава: Ярославъ — Yaroslav (gen. sg.); Yaroslav Vsevolodovich, prince of Chernigov (d. 1198), Svyatoslav's own brother — distinct from Yaroslav 'Osmomysl' of Galich addressed later in this part (unit 16), see note
былями: быль — elders, senior nobles (instr. pl.); an old word for a senior noble, cf. боярин
могуты: Могуты — the Mogutes (instr. pl.); an auxiliary light-cavalry group of Chernigov, of non-Slavic, probably Turkic origin, otherwise unattested (see note)
татраны: Татраны — the Tatrans (instr. pl.); ditto, otherwise unattested (see note)
шельбиры: Шельбиры — the Shelbirs (instr. pl.); ditto, otherwise unattested (see note)
топчакы: Топчакы — the Topchaks (instr. pl.); ditto, otherwise unattested (see note)
исъ: исъ — and with (prep.; = и + съ, a fused/variant spelling)
ревугы: Ревугы — the Revugs (instr. pl.); ditto, otherwise unattested (see note)
ольберы: Ольберы — the Olbers (instr. pl.); ditto, otherwise unattested (see note)
тіи: тъ — these, those (dem. pron., nom. pl.)
бес: безъ — without (prep. + gen.; spelled бес by assimilation before щ)
засапожникы: засапожникъ — boot-knife (instr. pl.); a knife carried за сапогомъ, 'behind/in the boot' (see note)
кликомъ: кликъ — with a cry, a shout (instr. sg.)
прадѣднюю: прадѣднии — ancestral (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with славу)
рекосте: рещи — you [pl.] said (aorist 2pl); Svyatoslav quotes his nephews' own boast back at them
му: мужаимѣся (as printed: му жа имѣся) — let us take heart, act like men! (1st pl. hortative, reflexive); the standard reading joins these three print-tokens into one word, мужаимѣся, kept split here as the 1800 print has it (see note)
жа: мужаимѣся (as printed: му жа имѣся) — let us take heart, act like men! (1st pl. hortative, reflexive); second of the three print-tokens usually rejoined into мужаимѣся (see note)
имѣся: мужаимѣся (as printed: му жа имѣся) — let us take heart, act like men! (1st pl. hortative, reflexive); third of the three print-tokens, carrying the reflexive ся, usually rejoined into мужаимѣся (see note)
сами: самъ — ourselves (nom. pl.); Svyatoslav quotes his nephews' own words
преднюю: предьнии — earlier, foremost (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with славу)
похитимъ: похитити — we will seize (1st pl. fut./pres.)
заднюю: задьнии — later, latter, remaining (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with an implied славу)
ся: ся — -self, reflexive particle (enclitic); placed before its verb, normal Old East Slavic word order (see note)
подѣлимъ: подѣлити — we will divide (1st pl. fut./pres.)
стару: старъ — an old man (dat. sg., short-form adj. used substantively)
помолодити: помолодити — to grow young again, regain one's youth (infinitive)
мытехъ: мыты — molt (loc. pl.); the falconry term for a bird's molt (see note)
възбиваетъ: възбивати — drives up, sends flying up (3rd sg. pres.)
ми: азъ — to me, for me (dat. sg. enclitic)
се: се — this (dem. pron.); also 'behold, lo' as a particle
уримъ: Уримъ — Urim (nom.); a genuine dark place, the word occurs nowhere else — most often taken as a garbled reference to Римовъ (Rimov), a town near Pereyaslavl recorded as sacked by the Polovtsians after Igor's defeat, but far from certain (see note); takes the plural verb кричатъ as a collective
володимиръ: Володимиръ — Vladimir (nom. sg.); Vladimir Glebovich, prince of Pereyaslavl, independently recorded by the Hypatian Chronicle as wounded defending his city after Igor's capture (see note)
глѣбову: Глѣбовъ — Gleb's (possessive adj., dat. sg.); Vladimir Glebovich, prince of Pereyaslavl (d. 1187), son of Gleb Yuryevich (see note)
всеволоде: Всеволодъ — Vsevolod! (vocative); Vsevolod III Yuryevich of Vladimir-Suzdal, later 'Big Nest' — a THIRD prince of this name in the poem, distinct from Igor's brother Vsevolod and from the Vsevolod Yaroslavich of unit 28 (see note)
ти: ты — for you, to you (dat. sg., enclitic)
прелетѣти: прелетѣти — to fly over, to fly here (infinitive)
поблюсти: поблюсти — to watch over, to guard (infinitive)
можеши: мочи — you can, you are able (2nd sg. pres.)
волгу: Влъга — the Volga (acc. sg.); the river
раскропити: раскропити — to splash apart, to spatter (infinitive)
донъ: Донъ — the Don (acc. sg. in unit 10, 'the Don... with helmets'; nom. sg. in unit 26, 'the Don calls'); the river
шеломы: шеломъ — helmets (instr. pl. in units 10, 22, 'with/under helmets'; nom. pl. in units 13, 29, functioning as grammatical subject — see note on the plural, not dual, ending of плаваша)
былъ: быти — had been, were (l-participle, masc. sg.)
чага: чага — a captive woman (nom. sg.); an old term for a female captive (see note)
по: по — along, over, according to; at, for [a price] (prep. + loc./dat.; sense varies by context)
ногатѣ: ногата — a nogata (loc. sg.); a small unit of the old Rus' monetary system, a fraction of a grivna (see note)
кощей: кощей — a captive man (nom. sg.); an old term for a male captive, from a Turkic word for a camp-servant/slave (see note)
резанѣ: рѣзана — a rezana (loc. sg.); a small monetary unit, smaller than a nogata (see note)
шереширы: шереширъ — shereshiry (instr. pl.); a genuine hapax legomenon, found nowhere else — proposals range from a kind of arrow or dart to an incendiary projectile, possibly a Turkic or Persian loanword; unresolved (see note)
глѣбовы: Глѣбовъ — Gleb's (possessive adj., acc. pl.); usually identified as the princes of Ryazan, sons of Gleb Rostislavich of Ryazan (d. 1178) (see note)
рюриче: Рюрикъ — Rurik! (vocative); Rurik Rostislavich, who held Kiev jointly with Svyatoslav in these years (see note)
давыде: Давыдъ — David! (vocative); David Rostislavich, prince of Smolensk, Rurik's brother (see note)
ваю: вы — of/for you two, your (gen./dat. dual)
плаваша: плавати — swam (aorist 3pl; agrees grammatically with the plural шеломы, not a dual form — see note)
храбрая: храбрый — brave (nom. sg. fem.; agrees with дружина in unit 14, with мысль in unit 20)
дружина: дружина — druzhina, war-band, retinue (nom. sg., a collective noun taking the plural verb рыкаютъ)
тури: туръ — aurochs, wild bulls (nom. pl., in the simile 'roar like aurochs'; cf. Vsevolod's epithet Буй Туръ, part 1)
ранены: раненъ — wounded (nom. pl., short-form past passive participle)
незнаемѣ: незнаемый — unknown (loc. sg., agreeing with полѣ); a recurring epic formula for a distant, unnamed battlefield
вступита: въступити — step! mount! (2nd dual imperative, addressed to Rurik and David)
за: за — for, for the sake of; behind, beyond (prep.)
русскую: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (acc. sg. fem., adj.); spelled with double с here, unlike рускую (single с) elsewhere in this part — a spelling variant kept as printed
буего: буй — bold, fierce (gen. sg., agreeing with Святославлича)
святславлича: Святъславличь — Svyatoslavich, son of Svyatoslav (gen. sg.); patronymic; spelled here without о after т and without ъ, «Святславлича» — the refrain's first and second soundings (units 15, 19), unlike its third and final sounding «Святъславлича» with ъ (unit 30) — a small, real spelling inconsistency of the 1800 print, kept exactly as printed (see note)
галичкы: Галичкый — of Galich (voc. sg. masc., adj.)
осмомыслѣ: Осмомыслъ — Eight-Minded, Osmomysl (voc. sg.); epithet of Yaroslav of Galich, first recorded here, generally read as praise for extraordinary sagacity (see note)
ярославе: Ярославъ — Yaroslav! (vocative); Yaroslav Vladimirkovich 'Osmomysl' of Galich (r. 1153–1187) — a different Yaroslav from unit 1's brother of Svyatoslav (see note)
подперъ: подперети — propped up (aorist 3sg / past active participle)
заступивъ: заступити — having barred (aorist / past active participle)
королеви: король — the King's (gen. sg.; король, ultimately from the name Charlemagne, applied to Western, Catholic monarchs — almost certainly the King of Hungary here, see note)
дунаю: Дунай — the Danube (loc. sg. in unit 17, 'at the Danube'; gen. sg. later in the same unit, 'as far as the Danube'); the river
меча: метати — hurling, throwing (present participle, nom. sg. masc.)
времены: время — times (acc. pl.); often read as a print corruption of бремены, 'loads, weights' (i.e. projectiles) — a genuine crux, kept as printed (see note)
рядя: рядити — ordering, arranging (present participle, nom. sg. masc.)
до: до — up to, as far as (prep. + gen.)
дуная: Дунай — the Danube (gen. sg.); the river
салтани: салтанъ — Sultans (acc. pl.); rulers of a Muslim state, taken as panegyric hyperbole about the reach of Yaroslav's power rather than a literal war (see note)
кончака: Кончакъ — Konchak (acc. sg.); the historical Polovtsian khan who, with Gzak, defeated and captured Igor in 1185 and went on to raid the Pereyaslavl region (see note)
кощея: кощей — slave-taker, captor (acc. sg.); reused here as an insult for Konchak himself, unlike its ordinary sense 'captive man' in unit 11 (see note)
рускую: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (acc. sg. fem., adj.)
романе: Романъ — Roman! (vocative); Roman Mstislavich, prince of Volhynia from 1170 and, from 1199, founder of Galicia-Volhynia (see note)
мстиславе: Мстиславъ — Mstislav! (vocative); a kinsman of Roman's from the same Volhynian branch, not securely identified (see note)
васъ: вы — your (gen. pl., possessive use, 'your mind')
плаваеши: плавати — you soar (2nd sg. pres.); lit. 'swim/float', of a falcon riding the wind
у: у — at, by, near (prep. + gen.); with ваю, 'you two have'
папорзи: папорзи — paporzi (nom. pl.); a disputed hapax — proposals include a mail neck-guard (aventail) fixed to the helmet, or alternatively straps/fastenings (related to поворозы) that secured it; unresolved (see note)
латинскими: латиньскый — Latin, Western European (instr. pl., adj.)
тѣми: тъ — by these (instr. pl., dem. pron.)
хинова: Хинова — Khinova (nom. sg.); an obscure, half-legendary distant people or land at the edge of the known world, also met in part 5 (dat. Хинови) — whether it preserves a folk-memory of the Huns or a later name for a far-eastern land is unresolved (see note)
литва: Литва — Lithuania (nom. sg.); a well-attested Baltic people, whom Roman Mstislavich is independently recorded as having campaigned against (see note)
ятвязи: Ятвязи — the Yatvingians (nom. pl.); a Baltic tribal group, close kin of the Old Prussians, settled between Poland and Lithuania (see note)
деремела: Деремела — Deremela (nom.); otherwise unattested, usually guessed to be another, smaller Baltic tribal group, but the name cannot be securely identified (see note)
своя: свой — his own; their own (acc. pl.)
харалужныи: харалужный — of kharalug [steel] (acc. pl., agreeing with мечи); the poem's recurring word for an especially hard, legendary steel (parts 2–5)
солнцю: сълньце — the sun's (dat. sg., possessive dative, 'the sun's light')
бологомъ: боlogo — good, weal (instr. sg.; 'не бологомъ' = 'not for good, inauspiciously')
рсіи: Рсь / Рсія — the Ros (loc. sg.); a river just south of Kiev, in the frontier zone exposed to Polovtsian raiding (see note)
сули: Сула — the Sula (loc. sg.); a river just south of Kiev, in the same frontier zone (see note)
храбраго: храбрый — brave (gen. sg., agreeing with плъку)
плъку: пълкъ — army, host (gen. sg., genitive of negation with не крѣсити)
крѣсити: крѣсити — to revive, to raise up (infinitive); cf. modern воскресение 'resurrection'
кличетъ: кликати — cries, calls (3sg); the Don personified, calling the Rus' princes to march (see note)
князи: кънязь — princes (acc. pl. in unit 26, object of зоветь; nom. pl. in unit 27, in apposition to Олговичи)
олговичи: Олговичи — the Olgovichi (nom. pl.); 'the sons/descendants of Oleg,' the whole Chernigov branch of the Rurikids, descendants of Oleg Svyatoslavich 'Gorislavich' (part 3) (see note)
доспѣли: доспѣти — have made ready, are prepared (past tense/l-participle, pl.)
инъгварь: Ингварь — Ingvar (nom. sg.); Ingvar Yaroslavich, prince of the Lutsk/Dorogobuzh line in Volhynia, grandson of Iziaslav Mstislavich of Kiev (see note)
всеволодъ: Всеволодъ — Vsevolod (nom. sg.); Vsevolod Yaroslavich, Ingvar's brother — a FOURTH prince of this name in the poem, distinct from Igor's brother Vsevolod and from the Vsevolod of unit 9 (see note)
мстиславичи: Мстиславичи — the Mstislavichi (nom. pl.); 'the three Mstislavichi,' cousins of Ingvar and Vsevolod, usually taken as sons of Mstislav Iziaslavich, from the same Volhynian branch as Roman (unit 20) — their exact identity is debated (see note)
худа: худъ — poor, mean (gen. sg. neut., agreeing with гнѣзда)
шестокрилци: шестокрилецъ — six-winged one (nom. pl.); most likely echoes the six-winged seraphim of Isaiah 6 as an exalted epithet, rather than a literal count of six princes (see note)
расхытисте: расхытити — you seized, snatched away (aorist 2pl; here for a group of five, carrying the plural aorist ending, not a dual — see note)
ляцкіи: ляцкый — Lyakh, Polish (nom. pl., adj.); from Ляхъ, the old term for a Pole (see note)
святъславлича: Святъславличь — Svyatoslavich, son of Svyatoslav (gen. sg.); patronymic; spelled here with ъ after т, «Святъславлича» — the refrain's third and final sounding, closing part 6, unlike «Святславлича» without ъ in units 15 and 19 — a small, real spelling inconsistency of the 1800 print, kept as printed (see note)
